privacy.description: What Grognard stores locally and what it only sends if you choose to use a networked feature.
privacy.summary: Grognard is mostly local-first in normal desktop use. Your files, databases, and settings stay on your machine unless you use a feature that explicitly talks to another service.
privacy.local_first: Normal editing, local entity databases, offline packs, and most settings remain on your computer.
privacy.documents_body: The user name you enter in Settings can be written into your documents as project/document metadata. That name travels with the file because it becomes part of the document itself, not because the app uploads it somewhere automatically.
privacy.github_body: GitHub sign-in acts as an identity key for the leaderboard and, when you configure them, for cloud backup and entity-database sync. A future version may also use it to store a corpus in a GitHub repository you choose. The OAuth token is stored locally and proves your identity; it does not give Grognard general access to your repositories.
privacy.ai_body: When you enable an AI feature, Grognard sends the passage being processed, your custom instructions, the target language, and the context needed for the task—including entity and date markers—to the endpoint you configured. With an online service, this data leaves your computer and is subject to that provider’s policies. With a local model, it is sent to the local server you selected and does not leave your computer unless that server forwards it elsewhere.
privacy.leaderboard_body: If you choose to participate in the leaderboard, Grognard sends the information needed to associate your progress with your verified GitHub identity and display a leaderboard entry. The exact indicators may evolve. Your text, XML files, and entity database are not sent.
privacy.telemetry_body: Grognard does not automatically send error or crash reports. To report a problem, use the project's GitHub Issues: https://github.com/grognard-xml/grognard/issues.
